title: Rehearsal
briefing: Optional specialism: business continuity. Valtren's business continuity plan was written three years ago and never exercised. You are asked to run a tabletop exercise for the executive.
Design it and run the debrief.

evidence.title: Current BCP
evidence.body: 62 pages. Contact list 40% out of date. Recovery time objectives set for IT systems but not for business services.

evidence.title: Critical services
evidence.body: Pharma deliveries, temperature monitoring, food retail deliveries, invoicing.

evidence.title: Scenario ideas
evidence.body: Loss of Northgate site for a week; regional power cut; key supplier failure.

options.label: Whether critical services can be delivered within tolerable outage times, not just whether IT recovers
options.feedback: Business services are what clients feel.

options.label: Whether IT can restore the critical systems within their agreed recovery time objectives
Whether the call tree works and the right people can be reached out of hours

questions.prompt: Which scenario do you choose for the first exercise?

options.label: Loss of Northgate for a week: it tests pharma, temperature monitoring and relocation together
options.feedback: Severe, plausible and exercises the most critical services.

options.label: A regional catastrophe that closes all six sites at once, to test the plan to its limits
A short loss of one system, so the first exercise builds confidence

questions.prompt: Which gaps did the exercise most likely reveal?

options.label: Out-of-date contacts slow the first hour
No outage tolerances for business services
Unclear decision rights between site and head office
The plan is too short
options.feedback: At 62 pages it is too long to use under pressure.

options.label: A short action plan with owners and dates, a two-page crisis card, and the next exercise booked
options.feedback: Exercises only matter if they change the plan.

options.label: A full exercise report appended to the BCP, for the auditors
A thank-you to participants and a note on the intranet: the exercise itself raised awareness

lesson: Plans that are never exercised fail. Test business services against tolerable outage times, fix what the exercise reveals, and exercise again.
